feedback.author: ChatGPT (agent; displayed author Jason Robey)
feedback.text:
Proposed — Reserve ten minutes for decisions and twenty minutes for documentation review.

Five minutes for decisions leaves twenty-five minutes for review, allowing broader coverage or closer inspection. It works when the remaining choices are few and straightforward, but leaves little room to compare alternatives, resolve disagreement, and record clear outcomes.

Ten minutes for decisions leaves twenty minutes for review: five fewer review minutes (20% less review time), but twice as much decision time. That gives unresolved choices and proposed next steps more attention, with the tradeoff that lower-priority documentation may need follow-up.

Recommendation: use the concise checklist to keep the first twenty minutes focused on the highest-priority issues, then use the final ten minutes to compare unresolved choices, record proposed outcomes, and identify owners for follow-up. If decisions finish early, return the remaining time to review. Avoid treating an unreviewed item as approved simply to finish the checklist.

feedback.author: ChatGPT (agent; displayed author Jason Robey)
feedback.text:
Proposed — Reserve ten minutes for decisions in the thirty-minute documentation review meeting, leaving twenty minutes for review.

Five minutes for decisions leaves twenty-five minutes for review, which suits straightforward documentation checks when choices are already clear. The tradeoff is a rushed close if disagreements surface, with less time to clarify rationale and record proposed outcomes and follow-up owners.

Ten minutes for decisions leaves twenty minutes for review: five fewer review minutes (a 20% reduction from twenty-five), but twice the decision time. Since the checklist explicitly includes unresolved choices, this is the stronger default. Keep the review focused on the objective and checklist, switch to decisions at minute twenty, and defer detailed edits that do not affect the choices. Use the closing time to record proposed outcomes, rationale, owners, and any unresolved questions; do not force a conclusion when evidence is missing.
